A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicPIG. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material retained or reorganized in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-estimation, downstream accuracy, ablation, and system-performance results, including 70B-model and reasoning experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds longer-context evaluations, model configurations, and hyperparameter and resource analyses in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects collision probability from 1 minus cosine similarity to 1 minus arccos(cosine similarity)/pi. This aligns the pseudocode with Equations 10–11, already correct in v1; the sampling design, estimator, centering, and CPU–GPU partition remain unchanged. An implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 extends RULER accuracy evaluation beyond the previous 16K–96K range to 128K and 256K inputs, adding longer-input test conditions. The benchmark families and underlying tasks remain unchanged; reasoning coverage was already present in v1.

E2.justification: Matching accuracy comparisons retain full attention and Quest, including the existing page-size variants. System comparisons retain GPU or CPU full attention, while TopK and oracle sampling remain in diagnostic and reasoning experiments. Newly cited methods are not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 replaces L40/Gold 6338 with L20/8563C and changes the simulated 4090 setup and assumed CPU bandwidth from 100 to 150 GB/s. v3 also adds ProLong configurations, expanded 70B settings, controlled fixed-budget/fixed-L experiments, and throughput evaluation under a 200 ms latency constraint.

E4.justification: The centering and TopK analyses in Figure 9 are retained. Appendices D.4–E add extensive investigations of hyperparameter sensitivity, memory/computation overhead, parameter transfer across model sizes, and accuracy at matched computation budgets, including fixed-4%-budget and fixed-L ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix F's calculated standard deviations concern an illustrative sampling example, not uncertainty estimates for the reported experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds extended-context, ProLong, and hyperparameter/resource results. The 70B 64K scores change from 88.4 to 89.2 for full attention and from 88.2 to 87.5 for MagicPIG (10,150). Figure 8 replaces serving results, including A100 speedup 1.9x to 1.5x and simulated-4090 latency 110 to 54 ms; changed settings prevent interpreting these as controlled gains. Tables 1–2 and reasoning scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a uniform hash-occupancy assumption and derives a retrieved-budget estimate in Equation 21 using the existing collision model. The principal definitions, Theorems 3.2–3.3, and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise advertised throughput improvement from 1.9–3.9x to up to 5x and latency from 110 to 54 ms. The central contributions—limitations of TopK, sampling-based estimation, and heterogeneous LSH execution—retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Appendix E substantially develops the interpretation of sampling-quality, computation-budget, and hash-memory tradeoffs and explains parameter-selection boundaries. New Appendix G explicitly identifies insufficient CPU DRAM and lack of prefilling support as limitations, and discusses alternative hashing, pipelines, and GPU execution.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents offline parameter selection, empirical budget mappings, model-specific hash-table/projector footprints, computation overheads, and 32-bit indexing beyond 64K. Section 4.4 revises reported projector memory from 25 MB to about 400 KB. Hardware descriptions are updated, and a project website is added alongside the retained code link.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for RetrievalAttention, ProLong, LSH tuning, advanced hashing, and GPU hashing. Attribution of expensive TopK search changes from Wu et al. to Liu et al.'s RetrievalAttention. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. v3 renames Section 4.3, reorganizes Appendix D, adds explanatory cross-references and appendices, and supplies an intuitive sampling example in Appendix F.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the title/abstract panel, headings, citation colors, and table highlighting. Figure 8 is replotted with revised axes and batch ranges, Figure 9 moves, Table 3 expands, and new extended-context and analysis tables are added. The existing reasoning table is retained as Table 6.

improvement.justification: The added controlled ablations, resource accounting, parameter-selection guidance, and explicit limitations make MagicPIG easier to assess and reproduce. New reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Table 3's ProLong full-attention average is 85.5 although its four displayed scores average 88.2, and Table 7's labeled latencies imply throughput above its stated maxima. The revision provides a useful net improvement, but the changed hardware and these inconsistencies limit confidence in a substantial overall quality gain.
